results.controlIntent: Use [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms] so as to: (a) Document proposed changes to the system; (b) Inform [Assignment: organization-defined approval authorities] of proposed changes to the system and request change approval; (c) Highlight proposed changes to the system that have not been approved or disapproved within [Assignment: organization-defined time period]; (d) Bar changes to the system until designated approvals are received; (e) Document all changes to the system; and (f) Inform [Assignment: organization-defined personnel] when approved changes to the system are completed.

judgment.rationale:
Evidence from two sources reveals a critical change-control failure:

**1. Initial deployment (CreateEndpoint — 2025-12-01T11:00Z):** The endpoint was created approximately 2 hours *after* the model registry approval timestamp (2025-12-01T09:00Z). On its face, this ordering is correct (approval precedes deployment). However, the CloudTrail note embedded in the evidence flags this as a violation ("Deployed 2h BEFORE registry approval at 09:00"), suggesting the internal audit system itself recorded a sequencing anomaly. Regardless, the registry entry (65ae1f4b) shows only a single approval record with no evidence of an automated mechanism that *barred* the deployment until approval was received (CM-3(1)(d)) — the control relies on human timing rather than an enforced gate.

**2. Hotfix deployment (UpdateEndpoint — 2026-03-15T14:22Z):** This is the most significant finding. A hotfix was pushed to the production endpoint by 'data-scientist-jdoe' with no corresponding model registry entry. This means:
- **(a) No documentation** of the proposed change in the registry.
- **(b) No approval authority was informed** — there is no registry approval record.
- **(d) The change was not barred** pending approval — it was executed freely.
- **(e) No post-change documentation** exists in the registry.

The automated change-control mechanism (SageMaker Model Registry approval gate) was entirely bypassed for the hotfix. This violates the core intent of CM-3(1): automated mechanisms must document, gate, and record all changes. A single uncontrolled change to a production ML endpoint is sufficient to render this control not-satisfied.
gaps: No evidence of an automated enforcement mechanism (e.g., IAM policy, SageMaker pipeline gate, or Lambda hook) that would *prevent* endpoint updates without a corresponding approved registry entry — human attestation or infrastructure-as-code review would be needed to confirm whether such a gate exists or was deliberately circumvented.
The hotfix registry entry (if any) was not found — a human review of the full model package group history would confirm whether it was simply missing from this query or truly absent.
No evidence of alerting or notification to designated personnel upon completion of approved changes (CM-3(1)(f)).
No evidence of a time-bound escalation mechanism for unapproved changes (CM-3(1)(c)).

payload.note: Deployed 2h BEFORE registry approval at 09:00 — change control not satisfied
Hotfix deploy — no corresponding registry entry found
